evaluation, as a part of the follow-up service, is the systematic collection and interpretation of data concerning the educational or vocational choices made by an individual in order to determine whether the placement services of an institution are being effective in assisting him in making those choices which will lead to his maximum benefit.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

placement and follow-up are inseparable in practice, that placement is an individualized process which is concerned with the matching of the individual and the educa tional or vocational experience, and that follow up is the evaluative aspect of placement which is concerned with determining the degree of educa tiona 1 or vocational appropriateness of the choices which an individual has made.

the role of evaluation, as it relates to the improvement of placement and follow- up, includes (1) the development of a sound conceptual framework for the services; (2) the identification and collection of the data which can provide valid evidence of the efficacy of these services; and (3) the interpretation of these data in such a way as to provide a basis for improving the quality and quantity of the services.

placement and follow-up are the two major phases of an integrated service which is concerned with helping the individual to make the decisions which will lead to the most satisfactory educational or vocational experiences possible for him.
The main takeaway from our work is that
we need to be more intentional about the evaluation of placement and follow up services in higher education.
evaluation is not a one-time, one-shot deal.
the placement and follow up services of an institution of learning can be evaluated only if the objectives of these services have been clearly and precisely defined.
